item.title: Couple accused of killing registered sex offender in pre-planned stabbing in Arizona desert
item.description: A couple allegedly planned the stabbing of a registered sex offender in a desert area in Arizona and now face first-degree homicide charges, police say.
item.content:encoded:
An Arizona couple was arrested after allegedly stabbing a registered sex offender to death in a desert area of the state, according to authorities.

Jacob Middlebrook, 35, and his girlfriend, Layne McIntosh, 36, were initially taken into custody for second-degree homicide in the death of 29-year-old Arron Christopher Warren, Bullhead City Police said on social media.

Police began investigating after a motorist found a dead man on the side of the road in the 3100 block of Silver Creek Road on Saturday. The circumstances surrounding the man’s death appeared suspicious, so detectives were called to the scene to conduct a homicide investigation.

MICHIGAN DECISION FORCES REMOVAL OF DISGRACED SPORTS DOCTOR LARRY NASSAR FROM SEX OFFENDER REGISTRY

Detectives later identified the man as Warren, a Bullhead City "transient." Detectives also identified a possible suspect and discovered that the victim’s vehicle was missing.

Hours later, Las Vegas Metro Police assisted Bullhead City investigators and located the victim’s vehicle parked at a casino in Laughlin, Nevada.

Middlebrook and McIntosh were taken into custody by Las Vegas Metro Police and booked into the Clark County Detention Center in Las Vegas, where they will be held until they can be extradited to Mohave County, Arizona.

On Monday, the pair's charges were upgraded to first-degree homicide.

CALIFORNIA SHERIFF FIGHTS PLAN TO HOUSE CONVICTED SEX PREDATOR NEAR GIRL SCOUT CAMP

Investigators determined that the two were also "local transients" who had known the victim for the past few months.

"Detectives discovered that the couple had expressed distaste for registered sex offenders and had planned the homicide in advance," Bullhead City police said.

"The couple reportedly pre-determined the desert location where they intended to leave Warren’s body. They also reportedly measured furniture/beds that could be large enough to cover the victim’s body along the side of the road. Warren was a registered Level 2 sex offender," the post added.

Bullhead City Police Chief Paul George said the department updates the community when certain registered sex offenders move in or change addresses but that he "will not tolerate anyone using this information as a reason to threaten, intimidate, harass or harm another person."

"When a Level 2 or Level 3 sex offender moves into our area or, more commonly, changes addresses, the Bullhead City Police Department shares that information as a public service to help keep residents informed," he said in a statement. "While required notifications are mailed to residents living within an approximate 1,000 feet radius of an offender’s registered address, we go a step further by sharing these notifications on social media to reach a broader audience. Our goal is to provide information, not create fear or alarm. We believe an informed community is a safer community."

"Our Bureau of Criminal Investigations conducts monthly address verification checks to help ensure registered sex offenders are complying with registration requirements. Our responsibility is to protect our community, keep residents informed and to enforce the law. We take all three of these seriously," George continued.

item.title: Newsom reveals when he'll decide on 2028 White House bid amid growing speculation
item.description: Democratic California Gov. Gavin Newsom says he will decide on a 2028 presidential bid by early January, but Kamala Harris could complicate those plans.
item.content:encoded:
Democratic California Gov. Gavin Newsom said Thursday that he will decide within the next two months whether to seek the presidency, revealing that he plans to make up his mind by early January about a potential 2028 bid.

Newsom, who will leave office in January, was asked about his presidential aspirations while attending the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Turkey.

"As it relates to 2028, we'll make that decision in the next few months," Newsom told Turkey's Anadolu news agency.

"I'll make the determination at the beginning of the year," he continued. "So we'll spend the next few weeks with the family and make a decision early January."

GAVIN NEWSOM SEEKS COUNSEL FROM ‘MASTER’ BILL CLINTON AS HE PLOTS PROJECT 2029

Newsom has long been discussed as a potential 2028 contender, frequently mentioned among possible Democratic candidates, including Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., and Sen. Jon Ossoff, D-Ga.

However, fellow Californian and 2024 Democratic presidential nominee Kamala Harris could complicate Newsom's plans if she decides to launch another White House bid.

Newsom previously said he would not run for president if Harris entered the race.

"I don't know if she runs, but we'll see," Newsom told CNN's Jake Tapper in a September interview. "But I wouldn't run if she ran."

"If she runs, you will not," Tapper responded.

NEWSOM ROASTED ONLINE FOR 'STAGED' FLY-FISHING INTERVIEW WITH CNN ANCHOR WHERE HE DROPPED MAJOR 2028 HINT

"Of course not. Why would I?" Newsom said. "I wouldn't do that to her ... I wouldn't do that to you. I wouldn't waste everyone's time. Who needs that?"

Newsom also suggested during the interview that spectators would feast on the "mutual-assured destruction" among Democrats competing for the nomination.

"I mean, you do whatever you want. I don't care," Tapper told Newsom. "But [the] counterargument would be, like, you know, she had her shot. And you've never run, and she's run twice."

"Yeah," Newsom responded. "I mean, that'd be the approach to the campaign, certainly. That'd be the case you'd make. Pretty good one, actually. That's objectively true."

KATHY HOCHUL ENTERTAINS MASSIVE POLITICAL PROMOTION AS DEMOCRATS LOOK AHEAD TO 2028

Newsom, who is term-limited after 2026, outlined his political timeline just over a week after Republicans suffered sweeping defeats in the midterm elections, losing control of both chambers of Congress and several traditionally Republican strongholds.

Newsom said he was "particularly pleased with the outcome of the election."

"Donald Trump's presidency, as we know it, ended last week in the U.S.," he said. "It was an historic rebuke of his tenure and now it's incumbent upon those that were successful to govern and to lead my party. The Democratic Party now has to set forth a positive alternative agenda to Donald Trump."

Fox News Digital's Joseph A. Wulfsohn contributed to this report.

item.title: Highly contagious bird flu detected in Wisconsin as officials euthanize infected flock
item.description: Wisconsin officials euthanized a backyard poultry flock in Rusk County after confirming a case of highly pathogenic avian influenza in the birds.
item.content:encoded:
A highly contagious strain of bird flu has struck a backyard poultry flock in Wisconsin, prompting officials to euthanize the birds amid ongoing concerns about the spread of the potentially deadly disease.

The Wisconsin Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection (DATCP) confirmed Thursday a case of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) in a backyard poultry flock in Rusk County.

Officials did not specify how the flock became infected.

DATCP said all birds on the property were euthanized and will not enter the food system.

H5N1 BIRD FLU CONFIRMED IN AUSTRALIA FOR THE FIRST TIME, MEANING VIRUS HAS NOW REACHED EVERY CONTINENT

HPAI, a highly contagious virus that is often fatal to domestic poultry, has circulated among wild and domestic birds in North America since December 2021, according to DATCP.

The disease is caused by influenza type A viruses and can vary in severity depending on the strain and affected species.

The virus can spread through contact with infected birds, wild birds or their droppings, as well as contaminated equipment or clothing worn by people working with the animals, according to DATCP.

JD VANCE INSTALLS CUSTOM CHICKEN COOP AT NAVAL OBSERVATORY AND WILL PERSONALLY CARE FOR BIRDS

When HPAI is confirmed in a backyard poultry flock, officials may establish a 10-kilometer surveillance zone, though surrounding poultry premises would not face movement restrictions.

DATCP urged livestock owners to take precautions to protect their flocks and herds, including washing hands, disinfecting equipment, restricting access to animals and separating new additions for at least 30 days.

The agency also recommended that poultry owners keep their birds indoors when possible.

item.title: Jayden Daniels throws three touchdowns as Commanders rally past Giants Thursday night
item.description: Malik Nabers and the New York Giants fell 24-21 as Jayden Daniels threw three touchdowns to rally the Washington Commanders in a key NFC East clash.
item.content:encoded:
Taking a cue from coach John Harbaugh’s stated goal of going 1-0 each week, Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers viewed Thursday night’s rematch with Washington as carrying extra weight after the teams tied last month in Week 5.

The Week 10 matchup was never tied, and Washington ultimately won 24-21, giving the Commanders a much-needed victory over their NFC East rival.

J.J. McCarthy made his first home start since joining the Giants in a late-September trade from Minnesota. The young quarterback played college football at Michigan under Jim Harbaugh, John’s brother, and finished Thursday night with one touchdown and one interception.

Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels threw three touchdowns and two interceptions at MetLife Stadium to keep Washington's hopes of winning the mediocre NFC East alive.

SUPER BOWL CHAMPION KYLE VAN NOY DETAILS WHAT REALLY HAPPENS WHEN A PLAYER GETS TRADED AT THE DEADLINE

Thursday's comeback win also moved the Commanders to two games back of the division-leading Giants and now own the tiebreaker after last month's tie.

Daniels getting picked off by Jevon Holland on his 208th pass attempt and Ar’Darius Washington on his 211th looked like it would haunt Washington, which allowed McCarthy and Isaiah Likely to hook up for a 66-yard, go-ahead touchdown midway through the fourth quarter.

But the Giants were unable to move the ball effectively enough on the ground to run the clock. item.title: Stephen A Smith debriefs interview with President Trump, warns Democrats face steep challenge
item.description: Stephen A. Smith says President Trump was "immovable" in refusing to accept blame for GOP midterm losses during their wide-ranging White House interview.
item.content:encoded:
ESPN commentator Stephen A. Smith debriefed his White House interview with President Donald Trump during an appearance Thursday on "Hannity" and cautioned Democrats over the influence of the party's far-left flank.

Smith said the pair discussed "devastating" GOP midterm losses during a 40-minute, wide-ranging interview and criticized Trump for refusing to take blame, saying he was "immovable" on that point.

"We talked about the devastating losses in the midterms and how the GOP essentially got slaughtered," Smith told Fox News host Sean Hannity.

"I asked him, is he willing to point the finger at himself, and he was dogged… he was immovable in that regard," he added.

DOUG SCHOEN: THE BIGGEST WINNER AND THE BIGGEST LOSER IN THE 2026 MIDTERMS

Trump repeatedly told Americans during his midterm blitz to vote as if he were on the ballot, but Smith said the commander-in-chief removed himself from that narrative during their Thursday interview.

"He said, ‘I wasn't on the ballot.’ I said, ‘That makes absolutely no sense, Mr. President. You said, put you on a ballot. That's what you told the American people to do.’ He said, ‘Well, they didn't do it.’ I said, ‘Well, what if they did do it and that was the reason you lost,’" Smith explained.

REPUBLICANS TURN ON TRUMP AFTER DEVASTATING MIDTERM LOSSES HAND DEMOCRATS CONTROL OF CONGRESS

"He refused to accept that," he continued. "His attitude is that the candidates were not that great. If it were him that was running, this would not have happened. That's his mentality."

Smith explained why he doesn’t agree with Trump’s perception of how the midterms played out and argued that the blue wave stems from Americans being dissatisfied with his presidency.

FOX NEWS VOTER POLL: 2026 MIDTERM ELECTIONS USHER IN A BLUE WAVE AS DEMOCRATS WIN CONTROL OF CONGRESS

"I think that he is somebody that is convinced his way is what it is. I just don't agree with him," Smith said.

"I think the American people made a statement against what they were seeing from him in terms of him not having his eye on the ball and coming across as a bit detached in their eyes," he added.

VANCE'S SCATHING IRAN WAR POSTMORTEM PUTS POTENTIAL 2028 GOP SHOWDOWN IN FOCUS: 'EVERYONE KNOWS WHY'

Smith told Fox News that Trump also gave him pushback when discussing the impact of the Iran War and tariffs on voter sentiment and the economy. He also addressed speculation that Trump offered him the role of White House press secretary.

"That was absolutely hilarious," Smith said. "Evidently, they don't know about the life that I live and the kind of affluence that ESPN and Disney have blessed me with."

"I wouldn't take that pay cut for almost anything but the presidency," he continued. "That ain't happening. Press secretary? Please."

Smith, who has lodged criticism at both Democrats and Republicans, warned that the Democratic Party faces a challenge from its far-left side.

"I definitely think that right now, the Democrats have a challenge on their hands because clearly there's a lot of people out there that view the Democratic Party as a divided party," he said. "Now they will tell you they're a very big tent and there's room for everybody, but I think that the progressive left has shown you there isn't room for everybody."

TRUMP SAYS HE WAS ‘ONLY KIDDING’ ABOUT MAKING DANA WHITE PRESS SECRETARY

"If you're not willing to capitulate to their desires, their wishes and their ideological beliefs 100%, then they got a problem with you," he added.

Smith called out Democrats who have declined interviews and expressed gratitude that Trump agreed to sit down with him for an interview.

"[Trump] was just very rigid and immovable in his thinking that it was blown by the people who lost and that the candidates on the Republican side simply were not good enough. It was not about him," Smith said.

"... I give him credit," he continued. "I asked a question, and he answered, and he didn't run from anything."

item.title: WWE star Brie Bella talks challenges of wine business, describes perfect Las Vegas day
item.description: Brie Bella reveals the financial mistakes and hard lessons that shaped Bonita Bonita wine ahead of her Las Vegas appearance at JP Brasserie.
item.content:encoded:
Brie Bella has proven herself to be more than just a WWE Hall of Famer. She’s a successful businesswoman and entrepreneur who has built up a successful wine brand with her twin sister.

Bella is set to make an appearance Friday at JP Brasserie and Sports Den in Las Vegas to celebrate the restaurant’s opening and help usher in the moment with Bonita Bonita wine. Fans of the former WWE Divas champion will be able to connect with her and enjoy sipping on a drink.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

Life isn’t always easy for a leader in business, especially if you don’t have the background in it. Everyone in that realm goes through the ebbs and flows of trying to build success and maintain it. Bella told OutKick Dropkick in a recent interview she’s certainly had to learn some things the hard way.

"I feel like, literally through my different business ventures, it's like I had to learn the hard way what people learned in business school," she said. "I mean, hiring employees and expecting people to have the same passion and vision you have for your company, it's like, no, they're employees, they're just showing up to work and they do a great job. And all of a sudden, it's like, awesome, the wine costs this, but no one told me the shipping would be higher in summer than it is in the fall.

"All these different things with budgeting and just the numbers was really hard on Nikki (her sister) and I at first, but we've been in the wine industry almost 10 years now, so, I've learned, I've made a lot of financial mistakes, I'm not gonna lie, but I'm now in a really good place and understand everything."

Being able to learn from those mistakes is crucial.

Bella learning from that and putting it in the rearview has helped Bonita Bonita thrive.

"Nikki and I, the big thing we do is we're always being like, OK, so the numbers, we didn't hit them this month, like, what held us back? One, is it because we didn't promote enough? Or two, is it because no one was filling whatever wine we put out," she explained. "We always like look and see like, how we're doing things, and then we switch it.

"We're going to be doing some different things in 2027 than we did in 2026, hoping we'd go up to the next level and I feel like that's what's helped keep Nikki and I afloat in the business. And too, we're really lucky that we have a millennial buyer. I mean, we have Gen Zs too, but like the millennials are everything, and they like to drink, so it's been good for us."

Bella will be at JP Brasserie and Sports Den, which she described as having a speakeasy type of feel to it and a place where patrons could feel warm and cozy.

But Vegas is not for the faint of heart – just ask my colleague David Hookstead.

OutKick Dropkick asked Bella what her perfect Las Vegas day would look like.

"Well, always a spa day, because the spas in Las Vegas are unreal," she said. "My favorite one's actually at the Wynn Hotel, because they have a cold plunge in their spa. I mean, you can do the works there. Nikki and I love it because then we'll get like the hydration IV. But for me it's a spa day. I love a really great dinner. Like, I want to feel like I'm somewhere else. I want all the details, I want the smells, I want the music. That's why we always go to Delilah's ‘cause you get some music, live music, and the food, everything in there is fabulous. And I love a show, a good show.

"I don't like clubs. That's why Nikki and I love JP's because we like a lounge. I can't have chaos. I go to bed at 10 p.m. When I'm home, I go to bed at 9, but if I'm in Vegas, I still go to bed at like 11 p.m. And so, for me, I want to feel a vibe, but I don't want chaos. So that's, that's how I enjoy Vegas. It's different than my twenties. Now that girl would have told you something way different."

item.title: Pete Crow-Armstrong unanimously ends Shohei Ohtani's run as NL MVP, Yordan Alvarez takes AL MVP for Astros
item.description: Pete Crow-Armstrong's 10.6-win season with the Chicago Cubs ended Shohei Ohtani's three-year MLB MVP streak with a unanimous NL award vote.
item.content:encoded:
Pretty much every season that Shohei Ohtani plays in Major League Baseball, he starts as the overwhelming favorite to win his league's Most Valuable Player award.

Ohtani in 2024 turned in one of the greatest individual years in baseball history, becoming the first player ever to hit 50 home runs and steal 50 bases in a single season. He won the MVP award. In 2025, he followed it up by hitting 55 home runs, stealing 20 bases, scoring 146 runs and, oh yeah, putting up a 2.87 ERA with 62 strikeouts in 47 innings. He won the MVP award. Unanimously.

All that's to say that it takes a special season by anyone to overcome Ohtani's unique contributions as top 2-3 hitter and a Cy Young-caliber pitcher on the mound. That type of special season is exactly what Pete Crow-Armstrong turned in for the Chicago Cubs.

CUBS LEGEND SAMMY SOSA SPEAKS PETE CROW-ARMSTRONG'S THREE-HOME RUN GAME AGAINST REDS INTO EXISTENCE

PCA, as he's more commonly known, was a top prospect in the Mets organization and had a solid 2024 as a part-time player after coming over to Chicago. In 2025, he demonstrated a rare combination of power and speed, with 31 home runs and 35 steals. But his swing and miss tendencies and low walk rate kept him from superstardom. That all changed in 2026.

Crow-Armstrong started slowly, but as the weather warmed up, became an unstoppable force. His walk rate skyrocketed from just 4.5% in 2025 to 11.4% in 2026. A jump in bat speed, from 72.7 mph in 2025 to 75.1 mph in 2026 proved vital, as his average exit velocity moved up over a full mph to 90.6 and his hard hit percentage increased to an exceptional 48.6%.

Those are good numbers and, surprise, surprise, as a result, his counting stats were outstanding. PCA hit a whopping 45 home runs, stole 41 bases, hit .280 with a .372 on base percentage and .570 slugging percentage. Offensively, he was 57% better than league average, and contributed his typically outstanding defense. Playing one of the most important defensive positions on the field, per FanGraphs, he was worth a whopping 23 runs more than the average center fielder.

Put all that together and you have a 10.6-win season. That's rarified air, and it paid off on Thursday night when he was unanimously selected as the winner of the National League MVP Award, officially ending Shohei Ohtani's three-year run.

HOUSTON ASTROS SECURE THE MOST EMBARRASSING KIND OF MAJOR LEAGUE BASEBALL HISTORY WITH AL WEST WIN

Very well deserved; PCA had an incredible season, and provides an incredible advantage for the Cubs with his elite offense and elite defense at a premium position while still under cheap team control.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

In the other league, Houston Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez, long one of the best hitters in the sport, finally got his league's ultimate recognition.

Alvarez, who's been a remarkable 66% better than league average offensively for his career, had a weighted runs created plus of 181 in 2026, where league average is 100. After returning from an injury-plagued 2025, Alvarez was a force of nature and arguably deserved even better stats, based on his quality of contact.

In an era where strikeouts dominate, Alvarez had 120 K's and 142 walks or intentional walks. His 33 intentional walks led all of baseball ... by more than double. That's the ultimate sign of respect from the opposition.

Alvarez hit 42 home runs, adding a .316/.432/.601 batting line, in an era of declining offense. That's a 60 run positive contribution to the Astros, without which they would never have reached the postseason. His 1.033 OPS was also far and away the best in baseball.

And again, he might have been a bit unlucky and deserving of even better numbers, somehow. Alvarez had a .429 weighted on base average, an overall measure of offensive success rate, but his "expected" wOBA was even higher at .442. Both, again, the best in the league.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

His "expected" slugging was a whopping .636, showing he had some extra base hits taken away by either quality defense or bad luck with stadiums. He too won first place in the voting unanimously.

It's rare that there's such consensus around the two MVP winners, but nobody seriously challenged Crow-Armstrong or Alvarez. And both were especially impressive results. Alvarez winning despite contributing nothing defensively, and PCA for overcoming the disadvantage that comes from playing in the same league as Shohei Ohtani.

Given their track records, it's a safe bet to assume that both will be right back at the top of the list for the 2027 MVP awards ... assuming there's a season.

item.title: DHS touts highest ICE deportations in history, as Mullin says agency has been ‘unleashed’
item.description: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin announced record ICE arrests and deportations in fiscal 2026, with arrests exceeding three Biden fiscal years combined.
item.content:encoded:
Immigration officials on Thursday announced a historic milestone, saying arrests and deportations this year reached the highest levels in the agency’s history, with arrests surpassing the combined totals of the Biden administration’s final three years and deportations nearly matching them.

"Fiscal Year 2026 saw the highest number of ICE deportations and arrests for any year in ICE’s history," Secretary Markwayne Mullin, Department of Homeland Security (DHS), said.

"The total number of ICE arrests in Fiscal Year 2026 was more than all three full fiscal years under Biden combined, as the patriots of ICE work around the clock to make America safe again. Thanks to President Trump’s leadership, ICE has been unleashed to target and remove illegal aliens so that we can save American lives."

Officials made more than 491,000 arrests, including nearly 475,000 administrative arrests, the highest administrative total in agency history.

MULLIN VOWS ‘ZERO CHANGE’ ON IMMIGRATION AFTER REPUBLICANS SUFFER CRUSHING MIDTERM LOSSES

ICE also carried out 483,200 deportations this fiscal year, surpassing the previous agency record of 442,640 set the year before.

Total arrests exceeded the combined figures for fiscal years 2022, 2023 and 2024 under the Biden administration by nearly 65,000, DHS said.

Meanwhile, deportations this fiscal year nearly matched the combined total for all three full fiscal years under Biden, falling short by fewer than 3,000, according to the department.

WHITE HOUSE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER TRUMP ANGERS BASE BY FLOATING ILLEGAL ALIEN DEAL WITH DEMS

Specifically, this year's arrests were more than six times higher than those recorded during former President Joe Biden's first fiscal year in office.

Deportations were also more than eight times higher for the same time period.

August 2026 also set a new record for arrests, with 50,925, marking the highest number for any single month in ICE history, Mullin said.

That pace continued into September, which logged over 48,000 arrests, representing a more than 300% increase over the average September under the previous administration.

Under Trump's leadership, more than 3 million migrants have left the U.S., DHS said.

As of October, the administration had deported nearly 1.2 million illegal aliens and arrested more than 1.25 million, according to the department.

"I couldn’t be prouder of the brave men and women of ICE, who just broke more historic records," Mullin said.

item.title: Dan Patrick concedes Texas ‘turned purple’ after Democrats’ historic blue wave
item.description: Outgoing Texas Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick says the state has "turned purple" after Democrats swept statewide races but warns the GOP must fight back.
item.content:encoded:
Outgoing Texas Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick, a Republican, acknowledged Thursday that the Lone Star State "turned purple" after Democrats' so-called blue wave swept statewide races and flipped the governor’s office, a U.S. Senate seat and Texas House.

During his latest episode of the "Lt. Dan Podcast," Patrick acknowledged that Texas’ political makeup is shifting left but stopped short of saying the state had turned blue after many others had described it as now a blue state.

"Right now, I’d say it’s purple," he said. "We've been winning consistently, and people see it as a red state. But this time, the Democrats turned out more of their Democrat voters than Republicans turned out of their voters. But what really made the difference were the independent voters, the voters who don't vote in Republican or Democrat primaries. They only vote in general elections.

"For almost every election, we’ve been winning those voters. We didn’t win them now. Will they stay voting for Democrats in the future? Two years ago, they almost all voted for the president. Four years ago, almost all voted for [Gov.] Greg Abbott, myself and the other Republicans. So, I wouldn’t say we are a blue state, but we’ve turned purple for this moment.

TED CRUZ SAYS 'BLUE TSUNAMI' TOOK OVER TEXAS AFTER DEMOCRATS SWEPT STATEWIDE RACES

"The wave election, a lot of factors involved from the top down, from Washington down to Texas and all the other states where Republicans lost," Patrick added.

"I would say it's a group of voters who are willing to change their vote election to election depending on how they feel and how they feel about who's in charge. So, we're not a blue state, but we're going to have to work too hard to be sure in '28 and '30 and '32 we don't become one."

Patrick, who ran for re-election but lost his race to Democrat Vikki Goodwin, was among the Republicans hit by Democrats' blue wave. Abbott, who was vying for a fourth term, lost in his re-election bid to Democrat Gina Hinojosa, and Texas Attorney General and U.S. Senate candidate Ken Paxton was defeated by Democrat James Talarico as part of huge Dem gains in the state and across the country, including in other traditional GOP strongholds.

Democrats won every statewide race in Texas, bringing an end to decades of Republican control in contests that had once been considered sure bets for the GOP and leaving Sen. Ted Cruz as the only Republican holding statewide elected office.

TRUMP'S GAMBLE ON KEN PAXTON BACKFIRES AS DEMOCRAT PULLS OFF HISTORIC TEXAS SENATE UPSET

Patrick said Republicans lost voters in places and demographics they had gained in 2024, including the Rio Grande Valley and young voters. He joined President Donald Trump, Vice President JD Vance and other Republican leaders in attributing the party's disastrous showing last week primarily to voters’ frustrations over affordability and the Iran war, which has caused soaring fuel prices.

Gas prices are about 83 cents per gallon higher than a year ago, according to AAA, which listed the national average at $3.91 per gallon on Thursday, compared with $3.08 a year earlier.

"We were in a tidal wave, a tsunami that washed across the country where people just said, 'I can’t afford to feed my family. I can’t afford to pay my bills. I can’t even afford to fill up my car or truck,'" Patrick said. 

"It was almost to the point where, no matter what our message was, it didn’t matter. People were unhappy, and I get it."

"People can agree with you on cultural issues or policy issues, but it doesn’t mean they’re gonna vote for you if they can’t afford groceries," he added.

Patrick further acknowledged that the war in the Middle East has increased the cost of fuel but refused to denounce Trump's decision to attack Iran.

"I totally support the president on that. If they had intelligence that Iran was gonna get a nuclear weapon, we could be in the middle of World War III if he didn’t take action, or Israel could have already been blown off the map," Patrick said. 

"So, I support what the president did, but the reality is that had an impact."

item.title: Van Hollen challenges Schumer for Senate leadership after Democratic election sweep
item.description: Chuck Schumer faces a formal challenge from Chris Van Hollen for Senate Democratic leader after Van Hollen accused him of siding with AIPAC.
item.content:encoded:
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., officially has a challenger for the mantle of Democratic leader, and incoming majority leader, in the Senate.

Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., who has become a progressive darling and outlet for those against Schumer’s bid for another term as top Democrat, officially announced that he was jumping in to challenge the longtime figurehead of the Senate Democratic Caucus.

"In this election, the American people called for change," Van Hollen said in a statement. "They called for a change from Donald Trump’s disastrous policies – but even bigger than that, a change from the status quo that isn’t working for working people."

BERNIE SANDERS SAYS HE WON'T BACK SCHUMER AS PUSH FOR NEW LEADERSHIP GAINS STEAM

"It’s now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need new leadership," he continued. "This is not about any one person – it’s about answering the call of the American people. That is why I’m running for Senate Majority Leader."

Van Hollen, 67, has served in Congress for 23 years, first starting in the House before moving to the Senate in 2017. Schumer, 75, has been an elected official since 1981.

The Maryland Democrat’s decision to run against Schumer comes after a listening tour with Senate Democrats, and follows his initial ambition of "kicking the tires" on jumping into the 2028 presidential conversation.

REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: A USER’S MANUAL TO UPCOMING LEADERSHIP ELECTIONS IN THE HOUSE AND SENATE

Since entering the Senate, Van Hollen has occupied Schumer’s left flank. It wasn’t until earlier this week that he fully took a shot at him, arguing that the longtime leader had chosen the "crypto industry," and the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) over progressive candidates that eventually won during this past midterm cycle.

But he's managed to capture some of the superstars of the Left, most notably Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed, who pushed Van Hollen to run. 

"The American public spoke clearly last week. They rejected Trumpism. But we have yet to earn our mandate. That will require bold leadership. I called on Sen. [Chris Van Hollen] to lead our caucus as a candidate back in April because he leads with courage and experience. We need both right now. Which is why I’m proud to stand with him in his bid to lead our Senate majority."

RACHEL MADDOW WELCOMES 'BIG FIGHT' BETWEEN SOCIALIST AND MODERATE DEMOCRATS AFTER MIDTERM WINS

Schumer did not take the challenge lying down.

"I welcome any discussion about the future of our caucus and the important work ahead," Schumer said on X. "I’m proud of what we’ve accomplished together—55 seats and counting is an amazing result—and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader."

"I look forward to leading our new Democratic majority and delivering for the American people," he continued.

Neither did his allies. Schumer has maintained since Democrats flipped the Senate that he would be the one to lead them over the next two years. And one of his possible lieutenants, Sen. Brian Schatz, D-Hawaii, who is vying to replace Sen. Dick Durbin, D-Ill., as Democratic whip, is riding with him through the storm. 

"Senate Democrats had historic victories last week, thanks to our talented candidates and the hard work of our caucus, led by Senator Schumer. And it was not the first time he has led this caucus back to the majority," Schatz said in a statement. 

"The American people sent a clear message: they want us to lower costs, end a needless war, and fight corruption. Our caucus has the right to have a conversation about the path ahead, but we have no time to waste," he continued. "We must move quickly to vote, unify, and get to work. I endorse Senator Schumer for leader and will be voting for him in the caucus election."

item.title: Toronto Blue Jays apologize after Muslim community outcry over Anthony Santander's Instagram posts
item.description: Anthony Santander has not apologized after sharing posts called Islamophobic, leaving the Toronto Blue Jays to issue a corporate apology on his behalf.
item.content:encoded:
The Toronto Blue Jays issued a corporate apology Thursday after activist groups targeted outfielder Anthony Santander over political Instagram posts he shared last week.

"We met with leaders in Toronto's Muslim communities today, who shared the harm caused by Anthony Santander's Islamophobic social media posts. The opportunity to listen and learn was important and reaffirms our beliefs and values as an organization. We condemn Islamophobia and all forms of hate.

We will work with leaders in Muslim communities to fight against all forms of hate. The Blue Jays will continue to ensure our organization reflects the inclusive community we are proud to call home."

Santander ruffled some feathers last week after progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's U.S. Senate race.

A native of Venezuela who grew up under socialist rule, Santander shared third-party Instagram stories, which included a thumbnail of El-Sayed reading "America voted for Sharia last night," a graphic stating, "Islam is not peaceful," and a preacher claiming, "there is no such thing as kind Muslims."

Santander deleted the posts two days later.

item.title: Donald Trump calls Barack Obama 'highly overrated' and claims he'd win a third-term matchup
item.description: President Donald Trump told Stephen A. Smith he'd "easily" beat former President Barack Obama in a hypothetical third-term election, calling him "overrated."
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump told "Straight Shooter" host Stephen A. Smith Thursday he believes he could defeat former President Barack Obama in an election for a third term, calling the former president "overrated."

Smith released an interview with the president recorded at the White House in which the two discussed several issues after the Republican Party's losses in the midterm elections.

During the interview, however, Smith floated a hypothetical matchup between Trump and Obama if they could both run for a third term.

TRUMP BRUSHES OFF REPORTER QUESTION ABOUT RUNNING FOR THIRD TERM IN 2028: 'THE LAW IS VERY STRONG'

"I got many more votes than he got, and I got many more votes in the states," Trump said. "And I have most of the state records of the big states. If you take a look at Texas, I have the all-time record. Florida, I have the all-time record."

"Are you saying you'd beat Obama?" Smith asked.

"Yeah, I think I'd beat him easily," Trump said. 

After seeing Smith's disbelieving face, the president added, "I think he's highly overrated."

OBAMA COMPARES TRUMP'S WHITE HOUSE RENOVATIONS TO 'SADDAM HUSSEIN OPENING A CHEESECAKE FACTORY' AT OHIO RALLY

When asked to elaborate, Trump explained that it was his opinion that Obama wasn't a "good president" and more of a "divider." By comparison, Trump claimed that he, as president, "brings people together" through mutual success.

Fox News Digital reached out to Obama's office and the White House for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

Obama remains a popular figure in the Democratic Party and campaigned for candidates in the midterms who went on to win their U.S. Senate races, including Ohio's Sherrod Brown and Michigan's Abdul El-Sayed.

TRUMP TEARS INTO STEPHEN A SMITH AS FEUD GROWS: 'ARROGANT FOOL, A LOW IQ INDIVIDUAL'

Later on, Trump asked Smith whether he would ever consider running for office, a prospect Smith rejected earlier this year.

"I would keep your life the way it is. You know what? You'll find it very nasty if you do," Trump remarked.

JERRY JONES GOES ALL IN AS COWBOYS TRADE FOR STEELERS' JOEY PORTER JR IN HOPES OF SUPER BOWL PUSH

item.title: Texas man executed for beheading 3 children: 'Going to be with my kids'
item.description: John Allen Rubio thanked loved ones and said he would soon be with the three children he killed before receiving a lethal injection in Texas.
item.content:encoded:
A South Texas man convicted of murdering three young children he helped raise was executed Thursday evening, nearly 23 years after the killings.

John Allen Rubio, 46, of Brownsville, received a lethal injection at a state prison in Huntsville, according to The Associated Press (AP).

Rubio was convicted of stabbing and beheading his children, Julissa Quezada, 3, John Esteban Rubio, 1, and Mary Jane Rubio, 2 months old. He was prosecuted alongside his common-law wife, Angela Camacho.

Rubio was pronounced dead at 6:47 p.m., 21 minutes after the lethal injection began, The AP said. 

OKLAHOMA MAN, 73, EXECUTED FOR PLOTTING MURDER OF LOVER'S HUSBAND, OFFERS NO LAST WORDS

The execution, scheduled for 6 p.m., proceeded without incident.

In his final statement, Rubio thanked his friends and family for their "love and understanding," acknowledged that he was "not the same person I once was" and expressed his love for his wife, according to the AP. 

"I want to say I’m sorry to my wife’s family," he said. "I can’t change the past, but I can tell you my life is going to be over. But that’s not going to make you happy.

"I’m going to be with my kids in a little bit," he added. "I’m ready to go to heaven to be with my lord and savior."

ALABAMA GOVERNOR COMMUTES DEATH SENTENCE AS DOUBTS EMERGE ABOUT EVIDENCE IN MURDER CONVICTION

The execution brought an end to a case dating back to March 11, 2003, when Rubio and Camacho killed their three children inside a windowless apartment.

According to court records, Rubio was not the biological father of the two older children but had nevertheless taken on a parental role in their lives, the outlet reported.

In the lead-up to the killings, Rubio reportedly claimed the children were possessed and cast himself as the "chosen one" destined to save the world.

Rubio at one point pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity. Defense experts reportedly diagnosed him with paranoid schizophrenia, but prosecution experts ultimately disputed the findings.

His defense team also painted a picture of a deeply troubled childhood, citing violence, toxic parents, drug use and prostitution as factors that stunted his development, the AP said.

Camacho pleaded guilty and is serving a life sentence for her role in the murders, according to reports.

The apartment building where the children were killed has since been demolished, and the property was transformed into a community park and garden, according to the AP.

Rubio's death marked the second of two executions scheduled in the U.S. for Thursday.

Just hours earlier, James Pavatt, 73, was put to death by lethal injection in Oklahoma. Pavatt was convicted of plotting and carrying out the 2001 killing of his partner's estranged husband.

item.title: Kirk Cousins expected a 'mature conversation' to get old Vikings No 8 back but got a big surprise instead
item.description: Jakobe Thomas refused money from Kirk Cousins for the No. 8 jersey, saying he just needs the Vikings quarterback to come back and win games.
item.content:encoded:
After Kirk Cousins was traded back to the Minnesota Vikings on Tuesday, the biggest question that needed an immediate answer was not whether he'd be the team's starter because that's the reason he was there, but whether he'd get his old No. 8 jersey back.

Cousins wore No. 8 during his previous six years with the Vikings before he left in 2025.

And this was a big deal for Cousins. He wanted the number and told reporters on Wednesday he would talk to safety Jakobe Thomas about getting it back since the rookie has been wearing it since he joined the team this season.

VIKINGS ACQUIRE KIRK COUSINS FROM RAIDERS WHO TURN TO FERNANDO MENDOZA AS THEIR STARTING QB

"I’m confident that Jakobe and I can have a healthy, mature conversation and figure this out," Cousins told reporters.

For those uninitiated in NFL traditions, this typically means a negotiation followed by a financial transaction.

The number in exchange for money.

Cousins made good on the promise to have that conversation by texting Thomas early Wednesday to see what it would take to make this happen.

Everyone figured that negotiation proved lucrative to Thomas because when Cousins came out for practice on Thursday, he was wearing No. 8.

And Thomas was wearing No. 6.

Except this is where Jakobe Thomas earns a grand measure of respect in the eyes of the team's new starting quarterback because he simply gave Cousins his number.

No negotiation.

No mature conversation.

"We trade, Kirko gets here. I look at and I'm just, 'Yup, he's probably going to ask me about it,' " Thomas said. "And I was just, 'He's got more memories with the number than I do and it's his number right now.' He's got more of a reputation than I do so let's just give it up."

"No money needed. I just need him to come here and win games. I don't want any money. I don't need anything. Just win games.

"...It's rightfully his."

This is class.

It is not cold-hearted business, but it gracious camaraderie.

Obviously, no one would have held it against Thomas to hold out for some money. Cousins, 38 and in his 15th NFL season, has made approximately $322 million during his career.

FERNANDO MENDOZA EMBRACES 'ONCE-IN-A-LIFETIME' CHANCE AS RAIDERS' QB1, CREDITS KIRK COUSINS' MENTORSHIP

Thomas, on his first NFL contract, is making $1.32 million this season.

But what is the price of respect that Thomas has earned from Cousins? Probably priceless.

item.title: Protecting failing schools and supporting teachers unions is not a winnable strategy, CEO warns
item.description: Tommy Schultz of the American Federation for Children says Democrats' reliance on teachers unions and opposition to school choice is a losing strategy.
item.content:encoded:
Democrats’ reliance on teachers union support and allegiance to underperforming public school systems is a losing political strategy, according to Tommy Schultz, CEO of the conservative advocacy group American Federation for Children (AFC).

"At the end of the day, when you look at the long-term trends here for the teachers unions, they're in a pickle because more and more folks are listening to the politicians that have a vibrant education agenda," Schultz told Fox News Digital.

"And they aren't just saying, 'We want to block all possible options' because the unions really don't have an agenda other than, 'We want to keep your kids forced to go to the schools that we run and control,'" Schultz added. 

"It's not a winning message at the end of the day."

MEMBER OF LARGEST TEACHERS UNION IN US CLAIMS ORG IS 'NO LONGER FOCUSED ON CHILDREN,' ONLY 'POLITICAL POWER'

Teachers unions consistently oppose many school choice initiatives supported by advocacy organizations like the AFC. They argue that programs such as vouchers and education savings accounts siphon taxpayer funds away from public schools. Union leaders maintain those dollars should instead be directed toward boosting teacher salaries, recruiting staff and upgrading public school buildings.

Democratic candidates in gubernatorial, congressional and state legislative races routinely back education platforms aligned with teachers unions. Financial analyses indicate the nation's two largest teachers unions — the National Education Association (NEA) and the American Federation of Teachers (AFT) — have spent hundreds of millions of dollars in political activism, lobbying and progressive advocacy over the past decade.

While the NEA and AFT rank among the largest financial contributors to Democratic campaigns, both organizations have occasionally supported select Republican candidates in rural districts who advocated for state aid for underfunded public schools.

Tensions between unions and parents have intensified in recent years, fueled by concerns over learning loss after pandemic-era school closures. In response, Republicans have campaigned heavily on school choice, enacting measures to provide families with state-funded vouchers and education savings accounts to access private or alternative educational settings outside their assigned neighborhood districts.

WATCHDOG REPORT EXPOSES TEACHERS UNION 'POLITICAL MACHINE' FUNNELING MORE THAN $1 BILLION TO LIBERAL CAUSES

However, recent Democratic wins in key state races could create headwinds for the school choice movement. In Texas, Democratic Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa has signaled opposition to the state's school voucher program after defeating Republican Gov. Greg Abbott in the Nov. 3 election. 

Hinojosa's victory raises questions about the future of Abbott's signature school choice legislation, which established one of the nation's largest education savings account programs.

"Fundamentally, I think it's a knee-jerk reaction to the largest funders of the Democratic Party," Schultz told Fox News Digital. "The teachers unions, they bring in about $3 billion a year for the teachers unions — the two national unions and their affiliates. So, they're a real big driver of the primary politics and Democratic politics in particular."

The Texas Education Freedom Accounts (TEFA) program, created by the state legislature with an initial $1 billion allocation, expanded access to private school tuition and other approved education expenses for eligible families. The program allows parents to direct state funds toward alternative education options, raising questions about the potential financial impact on traditional public school districts.

Major urban school districts across the country have faced steep enrollment declines since the COVID-19 pandemic. Some large districts, including Houston Independent School District (HISD), have faced challenges retaining students amid changing enrollment patterns and competition from other education options.

DENVER MOTHER FIGHTS FOR HER DAUGHTER'S EDUCATION AS ADVOCATES MAKE NATIONWIDE SCHOOL CHOICE PUSH

Despite legislative hurdles in some states, Schultz expressed confidence that parental demand for school choice will continue to drive political outcomes.

"What we found over the last chunk of years is that when you actually bring a message of pro-school choice policies and a brighter vision of education — of what could happen to public schools and for families controlling their child's educational destiny — those candidates win," Schultz said.

The AFT and Hinojosa did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

The NEA provided Fox News Digital with a statement it released after the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

"Across the nation, most Americans want the same thing — a more affordable future, strong public schools and safer communities. And they’re ready to slam the door on corruption and self-dealing," National Education Association President Princess Moss said.

"Tonight, voters came together across race, place and gender and sent a clear message and mandate: put working families, students and educators first and deliver for our communities, not billionaires and corporations."

item.title: Houston Rockets guard Marcus Smart handed 3-game ban after swinging at Warriors center Charles Bassey
item.description: Marcus Smart faces a three-game NBA suspension after punching Golden State Warriors center Charles Bassey in Houston's 115-108 win over Golden State.
item.content:encoded:
A late-game punch just cost Marcus Smart three games. The NBA suspended the Houston Rockets guard without pay on Thursday after swinging at, then grazing, Golden State Warriors center Charles Bassey.

Doing the exact opposite of his last name, the 32-year-old former Defensive Player of the Year melted down in the third quarter of Houston's 115-108 win.

Smart and Bassey got tied up fighting for position under the glass, barked at each other trailing the play, and Smart uncorked a right hook that grazed Bassey's nose. Teammates, coaches, and officials quickly stepped between them.

Smart did not wait for the replay review to finish before walking toward the locker room. Referees assessed him a Flagrant 2 foul and the 13th ejection of his career, ending his night with six points, two rebounds, and one assist in 17 minutes. He will sit out Friday's home matchup against the Utah Jazz, Sunday's road game in Washington and Monday's trip to Miami before becoming eligible to return Nov. 18 against the Indiana Pacers.

After the game, Rockets head coach Ime Udoka relayed Smart's excuse for throwing hands.

FAN EJECTED FROM NBA GAME AFTER HITTING FEMALE REF WITH BALL AS MELODRAMATIC LAKERS STAR THROWS TANTRUM

According to Udoka, Smart claimed Bassey wrapped up Smart's previously injured elbow during the tangle.

When Smart confronted him about it, Bassey allegedly replied, "What you gonna do?"

"And he did it," Udoka told reporters.

Bassey, who finished with seven points and six rebounds in 13 minutes, was unimpressed by the swing and unloaded on Smart in the locker room.

Bassey accused Smart of playing dirty all night, alleging the guard grabbed his knee while Bassey tried to set a screen in the first half. Bassey admitted he baited Smart into reacting and dismissed the punch as an excuse to clock out early.

"I knew he was gonna do something," he said. "I baited for him to do something, because I knew he was going to do something. I don't think he was trying to play. I think he was trying to get himself out of the game. He wasn't trying to play … I think he was trying to chill. He wasn't trying to hoop, bro."

The ban marks the third NBA suspension of Smart's 13-year career, following one-game league bans for hitting Matt Bonner in 2015 and threatening an official in 2021, plus more than a dozen fines that include a $50,000 penalty for shoving Joel Embiid in 2019.

Houston still closed out the seven-point win, but Smart's thin skin will cost him three games and six figures.

item.title: Super Bowl champion Kyle Van Noy details what really happens when a player gets traded at the deadline
item.description: Super Bowl champion Kyle Van Noy revealed the behind-the-scenes chaos of his 2016 trade from the Detroit Lions to the New England Patriots.
item.content:encoded:
Ever wonder what it’s like to be traded in the NFL midseason? Well, if you have, you are in luck.

Super Bowl champion Kyle Van Noy, who currently plays for the Minnesota Vikings, took to social media to share his experience of being traded at the deadline. The 35-year-old was traded from the Detroit Lions to the New England Patriots in 2016.

"I got a call from the Lions GM at the time saying I was traded (he forgot to tell me until the end of the call where I was traded to). You then get a call from the team that traded for you (patriots). They set a flight up with you as fast as possible," Van Noy said on X.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

He explained that the team that acquires a player wants to bring him in as fast as possible to complete a physical. Van Noy said teams want to avoid a situation like the one involving Maxx Crosby during the offseason, when the Baltimore Ravens backed out of a trade days after agreeing to it with the Las Vegas Raiders because of concerns about his physical.

Van Noy said teams will help players with some moving and living arrangements after a trade.

"The only thing when I was traded the team took care of was moving. Teams give you a certain amount of money for movers and shipping your car. Lastly, team takes care of about 10 days or 2 weeks paid for a hotel room until you can find your own living," Van Noy said.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

However, when it comes to a player's previous residence, they are responsible for handling those arrangements themselves.

"You can sell the house with a realtor if you bought one in the city you play in or renting you gotta pay the rest of the rent even if you are not living in it," Van Noy said.

Van Noy hasn't been traded midseason since 2016 and said things could have changed since then, but he believes the process remains largely the same.

Van Noy is in his 13th NFL season and his first with the Vikings. He has played for six different teams during his career. He spent the first two and a half seasons of his career with the Lions before being traded to the Patriots, where he spent three and a half seasons.

He was with the Miami Dolphins for one season before returning to the Patriots. Van Noy then signed with the Los Angeles Chargers, where he spent one season before playing the following three seasons with the Baltimore Ravens.

In his first season with the Vikings, he has recorded 15 total tackles and 1.5 sacks in eight games.

English model and former F1 grid girl Leilani Dowding has long been a supporter of bringing the models back to the Formula 1 racetrack. They were removed from the sport prior to the 2018 season in a move she's never understood.

It was argued at the time that the models no longer aligned with its brand values. The 46-year-old model disagreed with the decision then and she still does. She was in Los Angeles when the news broke and found out about it in the papers.

"I thought it was crazy. I remember thinking, 'what is going on?' It was always really welcoming," she told GrandPrix247 in a recent interview.

"The only people who would say stupid things, such as that we were being objectified, were people who weren't involved and had never spoken to us. They were looking in from the outside."

Dowding thinks the time for grid girls to return to Formula 1 is now. The modern, more entertainment-focused approach, especially at next week's Las Vegas Grand Prix, would be a natural fit.

She has an A-list actress in mind to lead the way and bring the grid girls back to Formula 1. The one and only Sydney Sweeney.

STEAMY SYDNEY SWEENEY AD DRAWS BACKLASH FROM FEMALE ATHLETES

"Sydney Sweeney would make a fantastic grid girl. I'd love to see her doing it for the Las Vegas GP, she'd be one of my favorites. She should get her boots on and get on that grid," Dowding said.

"I think she'd be wonderful. She'd make so many people angry, especially because you can just imagine them raging, with steam coming out of their heads."

Leilani Dowding doesn’t just want to see grid girls back in F1. She wants to take what the sport is already doing with celebrities and entertainment before the green flag and put it on steroids while ruffling a few feathers.

Dowding has a solid "Make F1 Great Again" plan if you ask me. All that's needed is for someone to implement it.

item.title: Ex-NBA player Gilbert Arenas responds to Steph Curry, stands by calling wife Ayesha a family 'blemish'
item.description: Gilbert Arenas offered a conditional apology on his podcast after Steph Curry posted a video defending Ayesha Curry against critical comments.
item.content:encoded:
Former Golden State Warriors player Gilbert Arenas clarified his comments about current Warriors star Stephen Curry’s wife, Ayesha, but stopped short of offering a full apology.

Speaking on his "Gil’s Arena" podcast, Arenas said his comments were intended to point out that Steph typically avoids controversy while identifying what he called a "blemish" on the Curry family.

"All I said is he doesn’t get in trouble for nothing," Arenas said. "He says the right things. If you gotta judge this family, his only blemish is what his wife said. That’s all I said. If there is a blemish, it’s that." The three-time All-Star later expressed regret if his comments offended Steph, but maintained that he had not intended them as a personal attack.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"I’m sorry if he’s offended. I didn’t mean it like that. I was just saying that he’s such a perfect dude… but I am sorry."

Nick Young, who is a "Gil's Arena" contributor, provided a more direct apology. "This man Gil won’t say sorry at all. I’m sorry, Steph. You my dog. I love you. If I offended you, I apologize like a man. I’m sorry," Young said. Young was Curry’s teammate for one season in Golden State, winning the 2018 NBA title with the Warriors.

Former NFL player Emmanuel Acho also apologized to the Currys for comments he made on a separate podcast.

AYESHA CURRY SAYS HUSBAND STEPH CURRY'S NBA PREGAME HABITS INSPIRED HER MOVIE CHARACTER, RESPONDS TO BACKLASH

"When a man humbly comes to you and requests an apology, then you wouldn’t be ignorant to respond with anything else than I’m sorry," Acho said. "Steph, I’m sorry for not just offending you but potentially offending your wife. I’m sorry for how it may have made you feel."

Acho added: "I’m sorry for how it may have made you feel seeing headlines, commentary, all these things about your wife," Acho said, referring to the reaction to Ayesha’s starring role in the Roku romantic comedy "Second Chance Holiday."

"I’m sorry for the reactions it may have caused internally, vicariously among you, in your central and nervous system."

The string of mea culpas came to light shortly after Curry took to social media to address criticism of his wife of 15 years.

"Usually the noise doesn’t bother me, it doesn’t bother Ayesha, but this one in particular, when you’re trying to step on the accomplishments of my wife and, you know, obviously needing podcasts, tapings and topics and giving opinions on somebody else’s wife," Curry said in an Instagram video posted on Wednesday.

STEPHEN CURRY ISSUES RARE PUBLIC RESPONSE TO CRITICS, DEFENDS WIFE AYESHA AMID ACTING-ROLE BACKLASH

One scene in the film calls for Ayesha to kiss co-star Matthew Daddario, a moment that sparked debate and criticism among sports figures on social media.

"Nick, Gil, Emmanuel, and anybody else who feels the need to wanna have to, you know, jump in and give an opinion of something you don’t really know about, something that kinda speaks to a bigger conversation on how you view women in this world and what they’re allowed and what they’re not allowed to do."

After defending his wife, Curry closed with a pointed thank you to the critics for the unsolicited publicity.

On the basketball front, Curry is expected to miss at least two weeks due to an oblique abdominal tear. ESPN reported Thursday, citing sources, that the Warriors are anticipating the star guard will be sidelined for closer to a month.

Curry’s night ended early Wednesday when he left the Warriors’ game against the Houston Rockets with less than seven minutes remaining in the first quarter. He later underwent an MRI. Houston won 115-108.

item.title: Here's how bad the College Football Playoff's selection committee rankings actually are | Ian Miller
item.description: College Football Playoff poll has Miami Hurricanes ranked five spots too low and Boise State nine spots below where efficiency metrics place them.
item.content:encoded:
It's been two weeks of the College Football Playoff poll and two weeks of seemingly unending controversy.

What the selection committee values, playing in one conference, and what fans and other analysts value, seems to be two very different things. There are any number of rankings that are controversial, confusing, or downright inexplicable. And committee chair Hunter Yurachek's attempted explanations during the post-release interview have only served to make things worse, rather than provide clarification for their thinking.

But it's easy to complain, subjectively, saying that one ranking or another doesn't make sense or isn't consistent with prior thinking. What though, would be the best system for putting teams in order? Or at least, a significantly better one that doesn't overly rely on the often-misleading "eye test" and inherent biases from committee members.

NEW COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF POLL PROVES THE SELECTION COMMITTEE IS JUST MAKING IT UP AS THEY GO

Fortunately, some outside analysts have come up with their own way of comparing a more objective set of rankings to the committee's uh, heavily influenced poll.

ESPN's Bill Connelly created a blended set of metrics to better evaluate important performance metrics. Essentially using an 80/20 combination, with the 80 side being resume rankings, strength of record, the "football power index," and the 20 side being forward-looking ratings.

WE NEED TO ABOLISH THE CFP SELECTION COMMITTEE AFTER YET ANOTHER EMBARRASSMENT

These are opponent adjusted, and focus more heavily on underlying efficiency on offense, defense and special teams. That's a better methodology for predicting how teams perform moving forward, considering wins and losses are noisy and often influenced by fluky outcomes.

So how does it look?

Well, you'll be stunned to hear that, once again, a specific conference has received a tremendous benefit of the doubt that they do not deserve, and that the Miami Hurricanes can feel especially aggrieved with the treatment they received after taking their first loss. Here's the list, with the arrows representing the position these teams are in Connelly's rankings, relative to the playoff poll. For example, Miami at No. 2 in Connelly's list is five spots higher than they are in the actual rankings.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Pretty impressive for there to be just one spot that matches! This is just one set of rankings, not necessarily definitive, and others have different outcomes, but it's an indication of how the committee values things that they shouldn't, while ignoring things they should care about.

Unsurprisingly, Kentucky is the biggest "miss" by the committee, as the Wildcats are still getting an immense amount of credit for their "SEC" schedule, ignoring that their performances don't warrant it. South Carolina is eight spots too high in the committee poll, again, given a tremendous amount of deference to simply existing in the SEC.

On the other hand, Boise State is nine spots too low, because the committee is incapable of appreciating performances against teams that do not play in the SEC.

Indiana and Wake Forest are underrated, Alabama is overrated, surprise, surprise, and Miami's six spot drop after losing to Notre Dame looks even more absurd. What might be a surprise though, and what would create some controversy, is the rankings for Ohio State and LSU.

The Buckeyes and Tigers both now have three losses, but computer-driven metrics give them credit for how they've played, while being unaware of Julian Sayin's injury. Efficiency-driven systems are much slower to react to losses to good teams than humans are, and the Buckeyes' three losses have been to Texas, USC and Oregon, while their win over Indiana and dominance against other opponents like Iowa still pushes them into the top-15.

Similarly, LSU gets credit for playing well in losses to Ole Miss and Kentucky, putting them higher than the committee's ranking.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Overall though, there are nine SEC teams in the CFB playoff top-25 poll. Seven of them are higher than they'd be using an objective metric. Missouri sits at No. 28 in Connelly's rankings, and No. 22 in the poll. Just because. On average, even including LSU at -8 spots, the average miss per SEC team was 2.5 spots higher than their performance-based ranking.

That is the problem; the SEC has spent years building itself up through concerted marketing efforts, the people that run the sport believe them, for some reason, and then teams are rated based on inaccurate assumptions. That's bad! There are tens of millions of dollars and jobs at stake, and the committee's obsession with rewarding SEC mediocrity is jeopardizing all of it. And the very legitimacy of the process.

The worst part? If, by some miracle, the committee corrected for this bias moving forward, the SEC fans, boosters and commissioner Greg Sankey would be livid. Beyond livid. The complaining, whining, anger and press conferences would be relentless. Until they got their way again anyway.

Once you get used to privilege, it's hard to give it up.

item.title: Gal Gadot cheers new Skydance co-CEO for 'sticking up against antisemitism'
item.description: Gal Gadot nearly broke into tears presenting Skydance co-CEO Ynon Kreiz with the Simon Wiesenthal Center's Humanitarian Award for his stance against antisemitism.
item.content:encoded:
Israeli actress and former "Wonder Woman" star Gal Gadot nearly broke into tears while praising Skydance's new co-CEO, Ynon Kreiz, for "sticking up against antisemitism" during the Simon Wiesenthal Center’s Humanitarian Award Dinner Wednesday.

Gadot joined movie producer Jeffrey Katzenberg and Skydance chairman and CEO David Ellison in presenting Kreiz with the 2026 Humanitarian Award. While presenting the award, she expressed horror at the rise of bigotry against Jewish people since 2023.

"I’m frightened by how quickly hatred of Jews is spreading and how openly it is expressed and accepted," Gadot said, according to Variety. 

"Since the Oct. 7 massacre and the war that followed, I have found myself asking how far this can go. If people get used to hearing and seeing hatred and looking the other way, then where does it end?"

ISRAELI ACTRESS CALLS OUT HOLLYWOOD STARS 'SILENCING ARTISTS' WHO SUPPORT JEWISH STATE

Gadot, who is Jewish, has long defended Israel after the deadly Oct. 7 Hamas attacks and praised Kreiz for his leadership amid the rise of antisemitism.

"What gives me hope is that people like Ynon aren’t wavering," she continued. "He’s doing what he’s always done. He’s standing firm. He feels what our community is going through. 

"He’s sticking up against antisemitism. He’s bringing his intense conviction and heart to this fight. He’s leading. That leadership is like a beacon of light and, in a dark hour, nothing matters more than a ray of light to give all of us courage."

Fox News Digital reached out to the Simon Wiesenthal Center and Skydance for comment.

MICHAEL RAPAPORT TELLS CRAIG CARTON THAT HIS SUPPORT FOR ISRAEL HAS COST HIM WORK IN HOLLYWOOD

After accepting the award, Kreiz, who is an Israeli, British and American citizen, thanked Ellison and Skydance for taking a "bold stand for Israel and the Jewish people" against what he called an "ancient hatred."

"We recognize that business leadership comes with moral responsibility," Kreiz said, according to Deadline.

Kreiz's award came just over one month after Paramount Skydance's $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. Before the merger closed, Ellison announced that Kreiz, who previously served as chairman and CEO of Mattel, would serve as co-CEO alongside him.

In a statement to Fox News Digital, the Israeli-American Council (IAC) congratulated Kreiz on the award and emphasized the need to speak up against antisemitism.

PARAMOUNT ACCUSES MARK RUFFALO OF INVOKING 'ANTISEMITIC TROPES' IN WARNER BROS DISCOVERY MERGER DISPUTE

"Gal Gadot is right to speak about the concerns around the spread of hatred of Jews," the IAC statement read. 

"No Jewish actor, writer, employee or student should have to wonder whether speaking about antisemitism or expressing support for Israel would cost them work, friendships or acceptance. 

"Opposing hatred of Jews should not require an act of professional courage. And when it does, something is deeply wrong."

item.title: Indie wrestling star Effy prepares for battle with Slade, fires warning to Dr Wagner Jr ahead of PRODUCE shows
item.description: Effy takes on Slade in a bloody bounty match in Kingston, New York, then battles Lucha Libre legend Dr. Wagner Jr. at Lucha Fresca in Brooklyn.
item.content:encoded:
Effy will be in the fights of his life this weekend as he has two matches on the docket as part of PRODUCE Wrestling’s back-to-back showcase in New York.

The 6-foot-2 superstar will face off against Slade in a bounty match in what will likely be a bloody affair for PRODUCE Wrestling’s Assembly event in Kingston on Saturday night. Then, in Brooklyn, Effy will take on Lucha Libre legend Dr. Wagner Jr. at Lucha Fresca.

Slade is someone who is going to bring the fight with him in every match he competes in and the two have wrestled before. He’s one of the toughest guys on the independent wrestling scene and isn’t someone to take lightly. But Effy knows that. The two have a long and storied history in which, according to Effy, led to Slade taking a hiatus from the ring for two years after one of their matches.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

He lamented having to take Slade off of his "chart" of pro wrestlers he’s faced and retired in an interview with OutKick Dropkick.

"I had to take it off my chart because there's been a list of people that have wrestled me and retired, and I don't think it's because the match was bad, I don't think it's because I ruined their thought of wrestling. I think they got in the ring, and there's a lot of perception about Effy, you know, you may have just learned a little bit about me, but there's 10 years of Effy you can go find where I've wrestled your Jeff Jarretts, I've wrestled your JBLs, I've wrestled your (Jon) Moxleys, I've wrestled your Jinder Mahals, all your favorites have come, through Effy and it's all there and, to now sort stand in this position where I can make or break a guy's life ‘cause they look in my eyes and they decide, ‘I don't know if I'm all the way committed to pro wrestling the way Effy is, I don't know if I'm ready to live this s--- all the time.’ I have people come talk to me and they go, ‘This isn't a character, you're Effy, you're committed to pro wrestling, you're in this.’

"Slade came back, and so I had to take him off my list to fight Slade again. And knowing what Slade puts up on the table … Here’s the thing I learned, you can talk to Slade all you want, he's gonna do whatever he wants. It's crazy. But now, I have history with Slade. I've been in there with Slade, I've felt him when he has the advantage of numbers, and now, if it's just me and him, I've got things to get out of my system, and for him to return to wrestling and for him to knowingly know, the last time or one of the times he wrestled me, he disappeared from this business for two years, they can say what they want about, ‘Oh, is Effy scared of Slade?’ But historically, I have made or break careers along the way."

Effy made clear there was no way he was going to miss Lucha Fresca in Brooklyn.

He detailed the list of historic Lucha Libre wrestlers he’s already put away in his career, including Pimpanella Escarletta and Psycho Clown. He was very much looking forward to beating Dr. Wagner Jr., especially in front of the legend’s sons.

"I thought he would have left after we found out he was a hot silver daddy when he unmasked and everybody could see him. I thought he would have gone into telenovelas, I thought he would've left wrestling, I thought he would've gotten the f--- out of taking bumps, but it's because of his stupid hot sons that he now wants to do more. We got El Hijo del Dr Wagner Jr., who is so hot. I got to see him in Tokyo, and I'm like, Jesus, this is before I've ever met Dr. Wagner. And then Galeno Del Mal, who is, I didn't realize how much I was into bears until I saw Galeno Del Mal, and he is just a thick muscle daddy, and so now you're letting me fight your dad?

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"I am going to make these boys think about things they have never thought about. I'm gonna make Dr. Wagner Jr. understand that Effy is a real-life Lucha Libre legend, whether anyone wants to admit it or not, and I will put him into a situation where he's going to have to decide how hard he's willing to get hit to get through Effy, and his boys are gonna watch me beat his dad up, and they're gonna come over and they're gonna have realizations about their life, and I'm gonna say, ‘No. Effy’s busy, you need to stay with your wives, you need to stay with them and stay away from Effy, ‘cause I'm only bad news, but I beat up your dad and I want you to know I would dominate you. I would dominate you in a way where I would make you my housewife and it would be beautiful, but I want you to see what I'm doing to your dad here and that I still give him mercy, because he is a legend, and I'm honored to be in the ring with him, but I want those hot sons to see what I'm gonna do to Dr. Wagner Jr. … Entering this match, maybe there's a little underestimation, but I think deep in his heart, Dr. Wagner Jr. knows the reputation of Effy, that if he doesn't put up the fight of a lifetime, I'm gonna embarrass him in front of his boys and his boys are gonna wanna sit on my lap."

It’s tough talk but that’s who Effy is. He’s one of the top independent pro wrestlers on the scene today as he was ranked No. 72 on Pro Wrestling Illustrated’s Top 500 for 2026.

Effy, whose real name is Taylor Gibson, opened up to OutKick Dropkick about being a gay man in a predominantly straight male sport. He enjoyed having the freedom to showcase who he truly is and putting himself out in there in pro wrestling in what he described as "an improvisational art form where I'm able to get with people and create almost a, a one-act play of a fight, a choreography of a fight scene that day and then perform it in one single take to a crowd with the goal being just to get them excited" without being restricted to a certain set of rules.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

He leaned into being himself and if the crowd reacted negatively to a gay man being in the ring, it was something he could lean into – yes, he’s a gay man, but also over 6 feet tall who could probably beat up almost anyone. He saw just existing in the ring may have been a beacon of light for others.

"I saw that me existing was sort of this little light in the corner of these people being able to come to shows. And so, as I kept traveling around, the word was spreading through the internet, through word of mouth of this wild gay wrestler, and people were coming to see it, not to try to attack it, but because they hadn't necessarily thought wrestling could look like that," he explained.

The success and the overwhelmingly positive feedback have allowed Effy to keep experimenting in the ring, pushing the boundaries of what a traditional pro wrestler is – even if it means spitting eggs into a competitor’s mouth.

"But that's so much fun that I get to go out here and see how that reaction goes, see what kind of press that gets, see what kind of internet breaking stuff you can do when you're given free rein to do it, and obviously, there's times where you don't do great, but the people that stick with you that go, ‘This is the kind of wrestling I'm attached to,’ and this is the kind of wrestling these fans are getting attached to, which is, it's a little dangerous, it's a little wild, it's a little over the top, it's a little extreme, and it's one of the few art forms where that's left.

"I'm excited that people have stuck with me this long and been excited because I've been able to just be myself unfiltered, and the more I've done that, the more I've trusted my gut, the more these people have found me or found wrestling in very strange ways, where there are things I've done where they get a million views and you go, that's something that I was just casually doing as myself and they're seeing it as, this is, ‘I had no idea this even exists. This is the craziest thing I've ever seen.’ And just being yourself and still getting those things to happen is, it's rewarding every time because I just feel fulfilled as an artist and those people continuing, they've kept me on this path to making it a career and making it viable and making it a living."
